title: Installment Payment Plans Cashiering Standards
content:
These cashiering standards state, for each of the **Installment Payment Plans**, which payment channels and methods are accepted, the largest single payment, and how a payment is applied and recorded.

## Channels and limits

| Plan | Channels accepted | Largest single card or bank payment | Personal check for an installment or renewal payment | Partial payment accepted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Point Paid-in-Full Plan | all seven channels listed below | 5000.00 | accepted | yes |
| Cardinal Point Two-Pay Plan | all seven channels | 5000.00 | accepted | yes |
| Cardinal Point Four-Pay Plan | all seven channels | 5000.00 | accepted | yes |
| Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan | all seven channels | 5000.00 | accepted | yes |
| Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan | all seven channels | 5000.00 | not accepted | yes |
| Cardinal Point Monthly Card Autopay Plan | all seven channels | 5000.00 | not accepted | yes |

The seven channels are the online portal, the automated phone line, a live representative by phone, mail, an agent office, automatic bank draft and card autopay.

**New-business down payment methods (every plan):** debit card, credit card, bank transfer (ACH), cash and money order. Personal checks are never accepted for a down payment.

**Partial payments:** a partial payment is a payment smaller than the minimum due; where accepted, it is accepted and applied.

**Mailed payments (every plan):** the postmark date of a mailed payment is recorded with the payment.

**Overpayment (every plan):** a payment that exceeds every billed amount becomes a credit applied to future installments, and any credit left is refunded when the plan closes.

## Order of application and the scoped current basis

The payment application order, the same on every plan, is: past-due invoices oldest first, fees before premium; then unpaid late and returned-payment fees; then the current invoice, fees before premium; then future installments, nearest first.

On a Monthly EFT or Monthly Card Autopay plan billing an Owner Auto Policy term, and only on such a plan, a payment is applied to past-due invoices oldest first (fees before premium), then to unpaid late and returned-payment fees, then to the current invoice, and whatever it leaves is held on the plan as a credit that its draft notices, or the first invoice after a move off automatic draft the named insured asks for, carry as their credit schedules set, an endorsement deposit and a switch down payment being held as their own schedules state; on any other plan, payments are applied in the order above, past-due invoices oldest first (fees before premium), then unpaid late and returned-payment fees, then the current invoice, then future installments nearest first, any excess being a credit.

For a Monthly EFT or Monthly Card Autopay plan billing an Owner Auto Policy term, and only for such a plan, a credit on the plan is carried onto its draft notices as the credit schedule sets, each installment is invoiced on its invoice date even when a credit covers it, and a credit still held when such a plan is moved off automatic draft to the Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan at the named insured's request is carried onto the first invoice after the move as that invoice's own schedule sets, that invoice being issued even when the credit covers it; on any other plan, and on a moved plan after its first invoice, credits on the plan reduce the next installments nearest first, and an installment fully covered by credit before its invoice date is not invoiced.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A customer on the Cardinal Point Four-Pay Plan with an unpaid past-due invoice and a current invoice sends 600.00: the past-due invoice is settled first, its fees before its premium, then any unpaid late or returned-payment fees, then the current invoice, and anything left reduces the nearest future installment.
